[h1]SUMMARY[/h1]
NES-Noir game ends before it even begins.

So, I wasn't expecting much. Bought this years back and it's been sitting on my backlog ever since...Maybe 2017, 2016? Anyways, I finally got around to playing it and boy, what a disappointment.

First off, there's 6 levels and 2 bosses, none of which are particularly challenging. The bosses I didn't die once on, and when I died on the levels, which are, at most, 5 minutes long, I started back at the beginning of the level. Once you get into the groove of the gameplay though, it shouldn't be a problem. The simplistic AI and mostly straight-forward level design keeps this from becoming much of a chore.

Where the game fails is the fact that it presents you with a connecting story that is left vague on purpose. Who are the baddies? Who is the guy that died in the beginning? Who are you? Why do you care? What does it all mean after you defeat the boss? None of this is answered, none of it particularly matters either. The level design on top of this is very basic, with very little of interest going on. For the most part you'll be jumping around samey-looking environments, sometimes with it venturing outdoors or underground, neither one being particularly unique.

Where it also fails is in its mechanics. You earn coins from crates and chests and some enemies, which you spend on ammo or health. Honestly, it felt like there could have been better uses for money, like on permanent upgrades. Perhaps buying increased health, permanent armor upgrade, larger magazine sizes, whatever, it just felt like it needed more to justify the money mechanic. As for the 3 weapons, once you start getting enough money for shotgun ammo and SMG ammo, you no longer need the pistol at all.

Generally not worth your time, even at only about a half hour in length.

[h1]OVERALL SCORE[/h1]
Not Recommended

[h1]REPLAY VALUE[/h1]
Light

Rot Gut benim sevdiğim iki tarzı bünyesinde barındırıyor: aksiyon platform ve noir. Steam indirimlerinde 4.52 TL param kalmıştı. Bir şeyler almak istiyordum. Araştırma yapayım dedim ve bu oyunu fark ettim. İndirime girmemişti ama olsundu. Bu oyun benlik bir oyundu. Oyunu aldım, oynadım ve şimdi sizlerle paylaşıyorum. 

Görsel tarz 1940'ların noir filmlerinden alınma, siyah beyaz karanlık bir dünya. Farklı bir deneyim sunuyor. Hikaye böyle bir oyunda çok beklenmez ancak ufak birşey yapmışlar. Her bölüm sonunda kısa konuşmasız ara sahneler giriyor.  Kesinlikle yeterli düzeyde. Oynanış öyle mükemmel bir kaliteye sahip değil ancak bekleneni veriyor. Platform kısımlarıda yine aynı şekilde. Düşmanlar eğer güçlüyse vur-kaç yaparak çatışabiliyorsunuz. Çeşitlilik 40 dakikalık bir oyun için gayet yeterli 3 farklı silahımız var. Ses efektleri ortalama. Müzikler ise harika müzik kategorisine girecek kadar kaliteli.

Kısacası "Aksiyon-platform severim" diyorsanız bakabilirsiniz. "Ama birde noir seviyorum" diyorsanız kaçırmamanız gereken bir oyun. Aslında oyun bittiğinde iade edebilirdim ama hem hak geçmesin hemde yapımcılara destek olsun diye yapmadım.

Итак, что же из себя представляет игра? Платформер, в лучших традициях старых игрушек про "Робокопа". Бегаешь, расстреливаешь врагов, собираешь монетки, на которые можно купить аптечки и патроны, и добравшись до финального босса угощаешь того букетом свинца. При этом игрушка достаточно легкая и позволяет из-за каменных стен расстреливать врагов. Не всегда и не везде, но когда такая возможность есть - грех не воспользоваться, верно? И да, игра щедро сыпет всем необходимым, так что если рука набита на платформерах из девяностых, то умереть страшной смертью вашему герою не грозит. Разве что... управление. Оно немного неудобно. Нет, передвигаться можно на стандартные W+A+S+D, а стрелять на пробел, но прыжки, на удобную кнопку я так и не нашел, поэтому пришлось играть со стандартным - прыжок на K, а выстрел на соседнюю L.  Да, неудобно, но учитывая общую продолжительность в 25 минут, пальцы не успеют устать. Приятная музыка будет отвлекать от сего просчета разработчиков, а глупые враги разлетаться от наших выстрелов, вызывая в памяти... хм, да того же "Чипа и Дейла", когда вместе с другом сидели в детстве и попинывали врагов, а порой и друг друга, под беззлобные подтрунивания. За что разработчиком спасибо.

Итог? Ищите игрушку на полчаса, что способна вызвать приступ ностальгии и желание установить эмулятор Дэнди? Что ж, вы ее нашли. Если же ваше детство/молодость случилась значительно позже и вы не застали 8/16 битные игры, то думаю и "Rot Gut" не сможет вас ничем зацепить. Так что исходите из своих предпочтений и будет вам счастье.

This is a fun little title, with simple controls, but very, very solid game play. Harkening back to the early 90s, Apogee side scrollers like Secret Agent. 

Game play isn't super complex, it's just jumping and shooting, but HOW the jumping and shooting works out is the treasure; Rot Gut will punish you for playing like a standard modern game, and expect you to be moving around dodging attacks while working in your own attacks at the same time; it's quite tight and well designed.

Absolutely worth the full price, and fun to boot up and give a whirl every now and then; this is for sure a title I will return to for fun, unlike most modern games, which I play and then put away.

Releasing a free to play game on Steam? Pretty sneaky. Let's talk about the merits of the game directly.

I blitzed this game in 18 minutes for 100% completion and I'm the kind of clown to sniff out every corner of each stage, mess around with all the items and die a few stupid deaths. Even for $2 that is a fridge too far. I'm all for blasting a game off the backlog with extreme prejudice but this is ridiculous. Rot Gut looks and sounds a little better than its weight class would suggest, the gameplay being pretty bare bones. There's some mild amusement to be had going through it once but there's no replaying this one or any deep systems to play at. The weapons and shops aren't balanced, bosses are simple jokes and the enemies are easier to run past than to fight. I don't usually give things the speedrunner approach on my first blind run.

Demo it in full for free on Kongregate and clear it in less than thirty minutes.

A very short game, the low price isn't even proportional to the content. There's only 6 levels which you can beat 100% with zero deaths in 30 minutes.

That being said the game has a very solid feel to it, the art style is very charming. Each level feels different and they're pretty neatly designed. Mechanics are very simple but require a bit of platforming skills to execute, which is fun, because the game gives you a lot of room with it's tight movement, air control and double jumps. Music is great too, certainly pulls some nostalgia strings there, bringing me back to games like Halloween Harry, Biomenace, Secret Agent, etc.

Overall I certainly wish there would be more of it, but it is also nice little treat on it's own.

This is an inexpensive little retro pixel action game which isn't too bad, but which is very short and has zero real replay value. The art style and graphics are simple, but nice. The sound is pretty good and the soundtrack is fitting for the genre. The gameplay isn't anything special. Run around, shoot gangsters and bad guys with 3 different weapons, collect money to buy ammo and health. It's not especially difficult if you learn to jump to the level of the enemies, shoot a few times, then jump away before they can shoot back. Those instances where you can't hit and run can be a bit brutal, but there's no real penalty for dying except for being sent back to try again with no loss of money. There are only a few types of bad guys with different firing patterns and the two bosses are very simple as well. The game... well, it has something resembling a story, but don't expect too much. 

I beat the game in less than an hour and there is no replay value. Frankly I should have beaten it in much less time than I did. You will get every achievement the game has if you beat it. There are no real branching paths or secrets to aim for. The game was decent fun, but it's impossible not to consider the value per dollar on it and in that respect it's pretty bad.

It's a very short but competent platformer/shooter. there is no controller support which is the way I would prefer to play a game of this type (and I did, thanks joy2key).  I really like the music here, it gives me Genesis vibes. I finished it in 30 minutes or so unlocking every achievement, no deaths. If you're looking for a challenge or a deep story driven experience, look elsewhere. If you want to breeze through a game and have a good time for half an hour, this is for you.

Rot Gut is a fun, simple and hard game. But when it gets you, it's over.
When you finish the game, that's it. You saw everything there was to see and did everything there is to do.
The last boss was anticlimatic.
This game needs a REAL final boss.
I liked the Robotnik-esque boss battles, but the regular encounters were more threatening due to the regular enemies aggressive behaviour.
The $5 slot machine was too generous.
It should have more Acts.
It should have more Bosses.
It should have more characters.
It should have more guns.
It should have joystick support.
It should have A SEQUEL.

Dev team, make it happen!
